items.explanation: index.html contains only an E-mail: label; its sole form has no Name: or Message: labels. contact.html has all three labels, but the check targets index.html.
In index.html the Earth row's row header is "Earth" and its Notes cell reads "Our world"; page copy "Earth is Our world" is not verbatim, but the row binds the fact.

risks.title: index.html form lacks Name: and Message: labels
risks.explanation: The only form in index.html contains a single label, "E-mail:", plus the email input; no Name or Message labels appear in that form.
risks.suggestion: Add Name: and Message: labels (with corresponding inputs/textarea) to the index.html contact form, or confirm that contact.html is the intended target.

limitations: Source reading only; no browser rendering, form submission or runtime behavior was observed.
The requirement says "Earth is Our world" while the table separates "Earth" and "Our world" into a row header and Notes cell; exact contiguous wording does not appear.
It is unclear from scope whether contact labels were intended on index.html or contact.html.

items.explanation: contact.html contains a static table with a footer SUM row (118) and purchase costs (30, 18, 65, 5), but no script, edit control or storage/backend code is supplied; recalculation after an edit and persistence across a server restart cannot be established from static source.

index.html table uses header cells with id/headers attributes for section, sub-column, country and city, and data cells list full header chains (e.g. antwerp belgium clothes trousers), giving each cell its row and column headers. The delivered CSS declares no keyboard focus handling; keyboard operability is not evidenced by static source.

limitations: No script or server-side files are in the inventory, so total recalculation and persistence after restart cannot be verified from source.
Keyboard navigation focus behavior and screen-reader announcements require runtime/assistive-technology testing; headers attributes only show declared source structure.
minimal-table.css contains no focus-visible styles; actual keyboard focus indication was not observed.
Rendered appearance and screen-reader output were not inspected; only supplied static HTML/CSS text was read.
